verses.text: Three days into his new post in the province, Festus went from Caesarea up to Jerusalem.
The chief priests and Jewish big shots brought their accusations against Paul to Festus,
asking him for a favor: bring Paul to Jerusalem. They were planning to take him out on the road.
Festus said no—the case would stay in Caesarea, and he’d be heading back there soon.
“So let your leaders come down with me,” he said. “If Paul’s done something wrong, they can charge him there.”
Festus stayed with them over ten days, then went back to Caesarea. The next day he took the judge’s seat and called for Paul.
When Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him, throwing out serious accusations they couldn’t prove.
Paul defended himself: “I haven’t done anything wrong against Jewish law, the temple, or Caesar.”
Festus wanted the Jewish leaders on his side, so he asked Paul, “Would you go up to Jerusalem and let me judge you there?”
Paul said, “I’m standing at Caesar’s court. This is where I should be tried. I haven’t wronged the Jews—you know that already.
“If I’d done something deserving death, I wouldn’t be ducking it. But these charges are false, so nobody can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
Festus checked with his council, then said, “You appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you’re going.” ⚖️
A few days later, King Agrippa and Bernice pulled up in Caesarea to greet Festus.
They stayed for a while, and Festus brought Paul’s case to the king: “Felix left this man locked up.
“When I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and Jewish elders reported him and pushed me to sentence him.
“I told them that Roman procedure doesn’t hand someone over to die before they face their accusers and get a chance to answer the charges.
“So when they showed up here, I didn’t waste time. Next day I took my seat in court and ordered the man brought in.
“His accusers stood up, but they weren’t bringing the serious crimes I expected.
“They were arguing with him about their religion and a man named Jesus, who died—but Paul keeps saying he’s alive.
“I was lost on how to investigate those religious disputes, so I asked if he’d go to Jerusalem and face judgment there.
“But Paul appealed to stay locked up until the emperor decides. So I ordered him held until I can send him to Caesar.”
Agrippa told Festus, “I’d like to hear this man myself.” Festus said, “Tomorrow you’ll get your chance.”
The next day Agrippa and Bernice arrived in full royal style. They entered the hearing room with the military commanders and city’s top people. Festus ordered Paul brought in.
Festus said, “King Agrippa, and everyone here, take a look at this man. The whole Jewish crowd has petitioned me about him, here and in Jerusalem, shouting he shouldn’t be alive.
“But I found no crime deserving death. Since he appealed to the emperor, I decided to send him.
“I’ve got no clear charge to put in my letter to my lord. That’s why I’ve brought him out here—especially before you, King Agrippa—so we can question him and I’ll have something solid to report.
“Sending a prisoner without listing the charges? That wouldn’t make any sense.”
